title: Indirect Statement with Infinitive
description: Used after verbs of saying, thinking, or believing (e.g., φημί, νομίζω). The subject of the infinitive shifts to the Accusative case unless it is identical to the main subject, in which case it is Nominative and usually omitted.

examples.translation: He thinks that the general is wise.
He says that he himself is writing.

mnemonic: Different subject = Accusative + Infinitive; Same subject = Nominative (omitted).

title: Purpose Clauses (ἵνα, ὅπως, ὡς)
description: Subordinate clause expressing intention. Introduced by ἵνα, ὅπως, or ὡς. Uses the Subjunctive mood after primary tenses and Optative (or Subjunctive) after secondary (past) tenses.
formula: ἵνα / ὅπως / ὡς + Subjunctive (or Optative) [Negation: μή]

examples.text: ταῦτα λέγω ἵνα τὴν ἀλήθειαν μάθητε.
examples.translation: I say these things so that you may learn the truth.
They fled lest they should die (so that they would not die).

mnemonic: ἵνα/ὅπως/ὡς + Subjunctive (Primary) or Optative (Secondary). Negated with μή.

title: Articular Infinitive
description: The neuter definite article (τό, τοῦ, τῷ) combined with an infinitive allows any verb phrase to function as a noun in any grammatical case, including taking prepositions.
formula: Neuter Article (τό / τοῦ / τῷ) + Infinitive Phrase

examples.text: διὰ τὸ μὴ παρεῖναι τὸν φίλον...
examples.translation: Because of the friend not being present...

mnemonic: Neuter article converts an entire verb clause into a declinable noun phrase.

title: Dative of Means / Instrument (Δοτικὴ Ὀργανική)
description: The Dative case without a preposition expresses the instrument or means by which an action is performed.

examples.translation: We see with/by means of our eyes.

mnemonic: No preposition needed for tangible tools or means in the Dative.

title: Past Contrary-to-Fact Condition
description: Expresses an unfulfilled condition in past time. The protasis (if-clause) takes εἰ + Aorist Indicative; the apodosis (then-clause) takes Aorist Indicative + modal particle ἄν.
formula: Protasis: εἰ + Aorist Indicative | Apodosis: Aorist Indicative + ἄν

examples.translation: If you had done these things, you would have erred.

examples.text: εἰ μὴ ἦλθον, οὐκ ἂν εἶδες αὐτούς.
examples.translation: If I had not come, you would not have seen them.

mnemonic: Past Contrary = εἰ + Aorist Indicative ... Aorist Indicative + ἄν.
